MEAT WORLD

By: Sasha Schwendenwein | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
We investigate a chain meat supermarket called Meat World. We discover they are changing sell-by-dates, are unhygienic and their products have micro bacterial counts in the millions!

Unique Selling Point:
In June a family came to Carte Blanche alleging that they had footage showing how a butchery/ meat market was:
1. Changing label dates (this is determined by the meat company – they go okay this meat can be packaged for 2 weeks before it goes off. So they put that label on: Expiry date: 14th, but then they try to take off the label and put a new one on that will then extend that date another 2 weeks – so it’s now outside of that company’s sell-by-date.) Our experts say this is fraud – and can be dangerous if the meat produce is an unstable product (mixed meat, pork/chicken/ sausage).
2. They re-wash and re-use poly-Styrofoam packaging/ trays (Experts say no amount of washing it with green soap will fix this – the bacteria’s don’t just go away and are often absorbed by the Styrofoam.)
3. They do not use hygienic cleaning products that they are supposed to use. Instead they use green soap (have photo’s).
4. They use sodium sulphate as a preservative. (This was made illegal back in the 1990’s – because it can cause cancer. South Africa follows the EU’s rules on food safety standards. According to our sources they use this in a bucket and paint it on the meat.)
5. They mix old mincemeat with new mincemeat (we do not have video of this)
The butchery/meat market were revealed to be called “Meat World”. They have 14 stores, their main branch is in Springs. The stores are franchised, and every store also has a manager. As observed in the video, many of the products are unstable meat products – vienna’s, sausages, wursts etc The owner of “Meat World” is a man named Angelino Periera. We will call him and ask for an interview.
The sources say they reported this to the manager of the branch, but no steps were taken. The source says they then reported it to the department of health, but nothing happened.
It’s important to also say that the video shows that this meat goes from the back to the front of the store, and the source is told that the “boss says they must do it.”


Summary:
About the sources: Bernard (father) and Jason (son- 22) both worked at the Krugersdorp branch for 3 months. Although initially, Bernard’s wife, Bonnie, was also working for Meat World as a cashier – although she was fired on her first day. She says a customer complained about her and was fired on the spot, without giving her side. Obviously that would have upset them, and she took her story to the bargaining council because she was fired and never given a chance to make her case. (we need to be harsh with them and ask them if they did these things.) Bernard has several accreditations as a safety and cleaning expert – he was working for Pick n Pay and then sent him on several courses. He and his family moved down to Durban and then moved back this year. There were no openings at Pick n Pay at the time, so Bernard took a job at Meat World. His son was working packaging meat with him up until he Bernard was given an offer to go back to Pick N Pay, where he is now.

Carte Blanche decided to do a process investigative. We wanted to see if their video and allegations were true. So we visited 9 of the stores and found “double label’s” at each store – we visited 4 stores 4 times and found double label’s at each. Not only did we find blood on the floors, meat just left in refrigerators, but we saw the employees handle the meat at several stores without gloves. We also noted that many of the fridges were not cold enough. At the main branch in Springs, there is no glass casing around the hanging meat carcasses, so anyone can sneeze on it, handle it etc… some products are not even kept in fridges. There are also large bins of sausages with no date – these are labelled R10 – if they aren’t sold that day, they still stay out there. Etc… We believe our sources are telling the truth from the evidence above. We then decided to take a step further… we have decided to test the meat.



Further information:
This took us 2 months – to find a SANAS approved lab willing to do the tests – we have their SANAS accreditation – they are doing this anonymously. There are very few players, and no one wanted to do it because they were worried the industry would take repercussions out on them later. We also hired a university student - masters of food science – at UP to accompany the producer to the different stores to ensure that we were fair to meat world – and meat world couldn’t say we purposefully touched or did anything to the meat. This was handed into the SANAS lab on the same day. All items were kept in cooler boxes and packaged and labelled. The results took 2 weeks – the lab says they tested some twice cos they were shocked at the findings. We visited 3 stores, and tested 7 products and 1 poly-Styrofoam tray.

Undercover video from source:
SEE THE STICKER
SHOW SELL-BY DATE (slow mo) A juicy piece of meat ready to braai is part of our heritage, and retail butchery group, Meat World, “place a strong emphasis on providing the best quality meat at the lowest price.” But, according to two whistle-blowers, to obtain those low prices, Meat World is allegedly extending the sell-by dates - sometimes by weeks - on processed meat products like Viennas, Russians and lunch meat.
Penny Campbell Penny: “That is illegal, you cannot misguide the public.”
PC Intro


Penny Campbell is the director of Food Control at the Department of Health. She says sell-by dates give consumers an indication of quality for a certain period of time, however, if meat is not appropriately handled, it can become contaminated with bacteria or pathogens like e.Coli.
Penny Campbell Intv
Penny: “The sell-by is usually provided when the retailer wants to provide the date, by which that food will reach the quality that that retailer has guaranteed.”
LINK Labelling law
John: “There are very clear standards governing the hygiene and quality of the food we consume, the legislation also states that the date marking on the labels cannot be altered or removed by anybody, and that doing so it is a criminal offence.”
Undercover footage from sources This cell phone footage of Meat World’s Krugersdorp branch was shot by one of the whistle-blowers who was in the presence of other employees, who he says were also relabeling products. The whistle-blower says they were told by managers to take expired stock off of the shelves; peel off the labels, thereby aiming to completely remove the sell-by dates; then, re-weigh the product, and cover the old label with a new one which carries a new price, but ALSO an illegally extended sell-by date. The products are then put back on the shelves for sale.
LINK Disposed of
John: “When the sell-by date or shelf life of a meat product expires, something which is self-imposed by the individual retailers, then the regulations are really quite specific, the product has to be disposed of.”

They say they told the directors of the branch, but nothing changed. Because the whistle-blowers are disgruntled; we needed to test the veracity of their claims independently.
LINK - Investigation John: “Because of the seriousness of these sources allegations, and because the reputation of an entire brand is at stake, we decided to conduct our own investigation. We visited 9 stores, over a period of two months, and could only move forward once we gathered our own evidence to back up the claims.”
5 stores: Kdorp, Centurion, CC, EP and Springs. 4stores: Edenvale, Alberton, Northcliff and Boksburg branches, At these 5 stores we found several examples of extended sell-by dates like this Kaiserfleisch lunch meat. But, at the other 4, while there was evidence of relabeling, we could not confirm if the sell-by dates had been changed.

We did enquire if there were complaints at the West Rand District Municipality about the Krugersdorp branch, they responded to say there are currently no complaints, and the store passed its inspection in May. While we don’t know whether this relabeling was to extend the sell-by date, the law says the date mark may not be removed or altered by any person. Both the Health Department and National Consumer Council say that illegally extending a sell-by date can lead a municipality to lay criminal charges or issue a fine to the company doing this between R1million and 10% of their annual turnover. To answer for this R1.5billion rand Franchise is Meat World’s CEO - Angelino Pereira. He says it’s grown to 14 stores in 22 years, mostly in Gauteng. HE OWNS a stake in almost all of them.

But in Pereira’s court papers earlier today, he complained that the footage in our story was illegally obtained. Carte Blanche denies this.

Shots of meat The whistle-blowers deny they sabotaged any equipment; however, independent of their information, we obtained our own footage from a number of other stores. We have more than 10 examples of where the sell-by date has been changed. There are also many examples of where there was evidence of a second label. A second label may have an innocent explanation such as re-pricing. We sent a random selection of mostly relabelled products for testing.
Link: link testing John: “We asked a SANAS approved lab to conduct a series of tests on our behalf, they asked to remain anonymous.”
Food lab – don’t look at lab shots
(CHANGE VISUALS) The lab feared repercussions from other clients in the industry. In order to secure the correct protocols for testing, we asked the University of Pretoria’s Food Science laboratory to assist with the scientific handling of the products. They advised on how the chain of evidence should be preserved from an independent scientific perspective and we followed this procedure. Several relabelled items were bought from 3 stores. While two of them did not carry a visible second label, they were all sent for testing to the SANAS approved lab.
LINK: JOHN IN FOOD SCIENCE John: “While test results might not definitively say whether meat has spoiled or not, they do provide an insight into the entire process, so a high yeast and mould content would point to a problem with hygiene, and that should always be taken seriously.”
Broll of Buys

Yeast and mould
We searched for an academic expert, Head of the Food Science Department at the University of Pretoria Professor Elna Buys, who has a doctorate in microbiology, interpreted the results for us. The Red Footlong Vienna’s from Comaro Crossing had a yeast and mould count of 78,000. The maximum the testing facility regards as safe is 1,000.
Prof and john intv august 18 – Comaro Crossing Prof: “That is totally not acceptable. And it would relate to definitely poor hygiene conditions.”
Prof Buys intv
Bacon bits
(august 18) Krugersdorp
NO PATHOGENS


This means that the processing environment where the meat was handled could have been unhygienic and led to the contamination. The draft legislation by the South African Bureau of Standards defines that NO pathogens should be present, but when we tested these bacon bits from Krugersdorp a count of 1300 coliforms was present. The maximum our testing facility regards as safe is 100. This budget Braai Wors we bought, also from Krugersdorp, did not carry a visible second label. As it was half frozen, we enquired if it was edible.

FAECAL CONTAMINATION
It had an e.Coli count of 310. Our testing facility regards a count of 100 as safe, although the SABS says NO pathogens should be present. e.Coli is hazardous to your health as it is as a direct result of faecal Contamination. So, the bacon bits or braai wors should not be consumed.
Angelino and john








Angelino: “I don’t believe we are selling products that are spoiled. It’s never been our philosophy or our belief to try and sell something that’s not correct.”
John: “But Angelino you say that, but the evidence is saying something else.”
Angelino: “Yes.”
John: “Your website says the same, “quality at an affordable price,” but what you’re actually selling is illness potentially, at an affordable price.
Angelino: “No, no that’s never been, we’ve never taken the quality and tried to take quality away from a good product.”
TWO WEEKS LEFT OF SHELF LIFE These 3 products which tested positive for pathogens still reflected at least 2 weeks more of shelf life, according to their sell-by dates. Professor Buys says Yeast and Mould, e.Coli and coliforms could lead to illness, and should NOT have been sold in the first place.
professor John: “Are they definitely going to get sick?”
Prof: “It is the processors responsibility to make sure that I, as the customer, do not buy a product that could potentially be at risk.”
Show cooking Professor Buys says ONLY in 25% of suspected food poisoning cases is the source of contamination determined. According to the Health Department, if the cooking of a product is not adequate, consuming that product could lead to food-borne illnesses.
Penny intv Penny: “Depending on whether or not you cook it properly, there is a potential, if there has been a pathogen in the product, to actually pose a health risk.”
An expert report given to the high court by Pereira questions our report’s validity. It claims that the samples we tested don’t match those purchased. SELL-BY DATE (slow mo) A juicy piece of meat ready to braai is part of our heritage, and retail butchery group, Meat World, “place a strong emphasis on providing the best quality meat at the lowest price.” But, according to two whistle-blowers, to obtain those low prices, Meat World is allegedly extending the sell-by dates - sometimes by weeks - on processed meat products like Viennas, Russians and lunch meat. Penny Campbell Penny: “That is illegal, you cannot misguide the public.” PC Intro Penny Campbell is the director of Food Control at the Department of Health. She says sell-by dates give consumers an indication of quality for a certain period of time, however, if meat is not appropriately handled, it can become contaminated with bacteria or pathogens like e.Coli. Penny Campbell Intv Penny: “The sell-by is usually provided when the retailer wants to provide the date, by which that food will reach the quality that that retailer has guaranteed.” LINK Labelling law John: “There are very clear standards governing the hygiene and quality of the food we consume, the legislation also states that the date marking on the labels cannot be altered or removed by anybody, and that doing so it is a criminal offence.” Undercover footage from sources This cell phone footage of Meat World’s Krugersdorp branch was shot by one of the whistle-blowers who was in the presence of other employees, who he says were also relabeling products. The whistle-blower says they were told by managers to take expired stock off of the shelves; peel off the labels, thereby aiming to completely remove the sell-by dates; then, re-weigh the product, and cover the old label with a new one which carries a new price, but ALSO an illegally extended sell-by date. The products are then put back on the shelves for sale. LINK Disposed of John: “When the sell-by date or shelf life of a meat product expires, something which is self-imposed by the individual retailers, then the regulations are really quite specific, the product has to be disposed of.” A0015 2.25 PEELS OFF LABEL WA0009 (slow mo) 2.45 – TAKES OFF LABEL - Label hidden camera whistleblower The whistle-blowers say they felt obliged to film the wrong doing, because they were concerned about public safety. They say they told the directors of the branch, but nothing changed. Because the whistle-blowers are disgruntled; we needed to test the veracity of their claims independently. LINK - Investigation John: “Because of the seriousness of these sources allegations, and because the reputation of an entire brand is at stake, we decided to conduct our own investigation. We visited 9 stores, over a period of two months, and could only move forward once we gathered our own evidence to back up the claims.” 5 stores: Kdorp, Centurion, CC, EP and Springs. 4stores: Edenvale, Alberton, Northcliff and Boksburg branches, At these 5 stores we found several examples of extended sell-by dates like this Kaiserfleisch lunch meat. Link – every single store John: “We needed to establish whether relabeling was limited to just one store, or was more widespread than that, but our investigation revealed that relabeling was happening at every single store, we visited.” Intro to Penny Director Campbell, who has a master’s degree in public health, says the relabeling of sell-by dates is serious. metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): We investigate a chain meat supermarket called Meat World. We discover they are changing sell-by-dates, are unhygienic and their products have micro bacterial counts in the millions!
metadata.Unique Selling Point: In June a family came to Carte Blanche alleging that they had footage showing how a butchery/ meat market was: 1. Changing label dates (this is determined by the meat company – they go okay this meat can be packaged for 2 weeks before it goes off. So they put that label on: Expiry date: 14th, but then they try to take off the label and put a new one on that will then extend that date another 2 weeks – so it’s now outside of that company’s sell-by-date.) Our experts say this is fraud – and can be dangerous if the meat produce is an unstable product (mixed meat, pork/chicken/ sausage). 2. They re-wash and re-use poly-Styrofoam packaging/ trays (Experts say no amount of washing it with green soap will fix this – the bacteria’s don’t just go away and are often absorbed by the Styrofoam.) 3. They do not use hygienic cleaning products that they are supposed to use. Instead they use green soap (have photo’s). 4. They use sodium sulphate as a preservative. (This was made illegal back in the 1990’s – because it can cause cancer. South Africa follows the EU’s rules on food safety standards. According to our sources they use this in a bucket and paint it on the meat.) 5. They mix old mincemeat with new mincemeat (we do not have video of this) The butchery/meat market were revealed to be called “Meat World”. They have 14 stores, their main branch is in Springs. The stores are franchised, and every store also has a manager. As observed in the video, many of the products are unstable meat products – vienna’s, sausages, wursts etc The owner of “Meat World” is a man named Angelino Periera. We will call him and ask for an interview. The sources say they reported this to the manager of the branch, but no steps were taken. The source says they then reported it to the department of health, but nothing happened. It’s important to also say that the video shows that this meat goes from the back to the front of the store, and the source is told that the “boss says they must do it.”

We wanted to see if their video and allegations were true. So we visited 9 of the stores and found “double label’s” at each store – we visited 4 stores 4 times and found double label’s at each. Not only did we find blood on the floors, meat just left in refrigerators, but we saw the employees handle the meat at several stores without gloves. We also noted that many of the fridges were not cold enough. At the main branch in Springs, there is no glass casing around the hanging meat carcasses, so anyone can sneeze on it, handle it etc… some products are not even kept in fridges. There are also large bins of sausages with no date – these are labelled R10 – if they aren’t sold that day, they still stay out there. Etc… We believe our sources are telling the truth from the evidence above. We then decided to take a step further… we have decided to test the meat.
